solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Deceitful cheat with quiet line

parts.note: ease is quiet, rest, tranquillity

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of being a dishonest cheat who keeps things quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneaky, untrustworthy person is called after the furtive little predator, so the animal's name serves as an insult.

clue.text: Frightening English series never succeeded

indicators.note: never means every S standing for succeeded is taken out of the word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies; both are dropped

explanation.surface: An English TV series that frightened viewers never caught on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never succeeded' removes both S's from SERIES, leaving ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncanny and spooky is unsettling, so it is frightening in a creepy way.

clue.text: Cook soup of red tomatoes, perhaps

indicators.note: to cook something up is to concoct it, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: make soup from red tomatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomatoes are among foods marketed as especially nutritious, an example of the category; hence the perhaps.

clue.text: Raised fish process margin of safety

indicators.note: Raised in a down entry means the fish's name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an eel is a fish
a way is a method or process

explanation.surface: Farmed fish production is said to have a safety margin.
explanation.definitionFit: Room for manoeuvre or tolerance against error is a margin of safety.

clue.text: Shakespearean heroine over-familiar Plantagenet king ravished

parts.note: Viola is the heroine of Twelfth Night
Ted is an over-familiar form of Edward, a name borne by several Plantagenet kings

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of a Shakespearean heroine assaulted by a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over-familiar' asks for a pet form of the king's name rather than the name itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravish is an old literary word for to rape, so the past tense matches the participle.

clue.text: A mullah's waiving broadcast for composer

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A mullah waives his objection to a broadcast of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Vaughan Williams was an English composer of symphonies and folk-song settings.

clue.text: Facing work to advance start of earning

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to posit is to advance or put forward an idea

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of the word earning is taken

explanation.surface: Facing work to get an advance before starting to earn.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things across from each other are face to face, so the word means facing.

clue.text: Following behind King Edward

parts.note: aft means behind, at the back of a ship
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Following behind King Edward in a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' is also a British potato variety, a red herring here.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming later in sequence is a synonym for following.

clue.text: Succulent fruit raised with input from unknown writer

indicators.note: with input from means the unknown goes into the reversed letters
raised in a down entry means the plant and fruit are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an aloe is a succulent plant
a lime is a fruit
Z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A succulent and a fruit grown with help from an unknown source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ALOE + LIME into EMILEOLA; 'with input from' then slips Z in, splitting the two names of the French novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist of the Rougon-Macquart cycle, author of Germinal, was a writer.

clue.text: A very stiff drink to start event

parts.note: a triple is a treble measure of spirits, a very stiff drink
to jump is to start in surprise

explanation.surface: Someone downs a strong drink before an event to steady their nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: The hop, step and jump is an athletics field event, so it is one example of an event.

clue.text: Suddenly get time before lecture

parts.note: to wig is an old British verb meaning to scold or lecture severely

explanation.surface: A student suddenly grasps the point just as the lecture begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply puts T ahead of WIG.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British speech, to twig something is to understand it all at once.

clue.text: Scold for getting in contact

indicators.note: getting in means the word for goes inside the word for contact

parts.note: to reach someone is to contact them
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for making contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word but is the inserted piece, the Latin-derived 'pro'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke someone and express disappointment in them is close synonym territory for telling off.

clue.text: Scream when green ogre catches one

indicators.note: catches means the ogre holds the numeral within him

parts.note: Shrek is the green ogre of the animated films
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone screams when the green ogre grabs a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud, high-pitched cry is a synonym for a scream.

clue.text: No information on fluorine, perhaps something good and light

indicators.note: No means the word for information is dropped from the element group

parts.note: fluorine is an example of a halogen, the chemical element group
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A chemistry note admits ignorance about fluorine.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN for information is British slang. The definition is cryptic: a saint's ring of light is both good and light.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of light around a saint's head signals goodness, so it is good and light at once.

clue.text: Capricious Rita messed with Barry

indicators.note: messed with means the names are jumbled up together

explanation.surface: Fickle Rita toyed with Barry's affections.
explanation.definitionFit: Decisions made on whim rather than reason are random and changeable, hence capricious.

clue.text: People keeping books as a way of recording things

indicators.note: keeping means the people hold the books inside them

parts.note: a nation is a people
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A people keep books as their way of recording history.
explanation.walkthrough: OT, the Old Testament, is the crossword's usual reading of 'books'.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of written symbols, as in music or chess, is a method for recording things.

clue.text: What could give you extra change? Yes, but most often no!

definitions.text: What could give you extra change? Yes, but most often no!

parts.words: What could give you extra change? Yes, but most often no!
parts.note: the form filed with the revenue might bring a refund, extra change, but usually brings a bill; the letters of extra plus a word for change also make the answer

explanation.surface: Wondering whether something brings extra cash, and concluding it rarely does.
explanation.walkthrough: A refund from the taxman is extra money, but most filings end in a payment. As a bonus, an anagram of EXTRA (TAXRE) plus TURN, change, spells it.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual declaration of income to the revenue can produce a rebate, though usually it does not.

clue.text: Removes wrapper around fish for help with stock control

indicators.note: around means the word for strips goes round the fish

parts.note: to bare something is to strip off its covering
cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone unwraps a fish for a shop's stock-taking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removes wrapper' reads as an action on the fish, but it is a synonym in its own right that goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Striped labels scanned at tills track inventory, so they help with stock control.

clue.text: State having a friend in America and a lot of dependency

parts.note: bud is American slang for a friend

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a habit is a dependency, as on a drug

explanation.surface: A state that has an American friend and depends on it heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims HABIT to HABI.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the seven emirates of the UAE, a constituent state with its own ruler.

clue.text: Times certainly is after right photograph

indicators.note: is after means the word for certainly comes after the abbreviation for right

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times
ay is an old or dialect yes, certainly

explanation.surface: The Times certainly follows the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiograph of bones is a kind of photographic image, so the word works as a photograph.

clue.text: Slough service carries soldiers

indicators.note: carries means the church service holds the soldiers inside it

parts.note: Mass is a church service
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A church service in Slough, the Berkshire town, includes soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' looks like the English town but means a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A swamp or bog is a slough, so a marshy quagmire fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Fantasy heroine abridged after appeal for emphatic writing style

indicators.note: after places the heroine after the word for appeal

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: abridged means the heroine's name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Alice is the heroine of the fantasy Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A fantasy heroine's story is shortened after public demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' drops the heroine's last letter; 'appeal' is sex appeal, old slang IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type is used to give emphasis in printed text, so it is an emphatic style of lettering.

clue.text: Output from auto industry keeps Britain in uncertain state

indicators.note: keeps means the car holds the abbreviation for Britain inside it

parts.note: a limo, a limousine, is a car produced by the motor industry

explanation.surface: Car output that keeps Britain's economy in uncertainty.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediate condition of waiting, neither one thing nor another, is a state of uncertainty.

clue.text: Spectator seeing throne with king and queen performing

parts.note: throne is jocular slang for the lavatory, the loo
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: A spectator watches a king and queen performing on a throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throne' is a joke name for the toilet, LOO in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who watches without taking part is an onlooker, the same thing as a spectator.

clue.text: Sulphur found in old beer, mostly stout

indicators.note: found in means the sulphur symbol is placed inside the shortened drink
mostly means the last letter of the drink is cut off

parts.note: taken as written
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Sulphur is detected in old beer, mostly stout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims BEER to BEE; 'found in' puts S in it, giving BESE after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout describes a heavily built, fat person, so it means very overweight.

clue.text: Buddy with male date?

parts.note: a pal is a buddy

explanation.surface: A dating question: is a buddy with a man a date?
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' is not a romantic outing but the fruit's tree; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: The date is a tree of this kind, so the date palm is an example of the family, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Hamlet's mother, say, is one that's shown stagy performance?

definitions.meaning: Gertrude is a queen who appears in a drama, a play
a histrionic person given to theatrical overreaction

explanation.surface: Gertrude is called a person who overacts on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a queen in a play, and idiomatically a person given to exaggerated emotional displays.

clue.text: Back in stables is pony safe? That's general view

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking whether a pony is safe in the stables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden run SISPONYS, which 'Back' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary gives an overview of a whole work, a general view of it.

clue.text: Boy going on to bask under the water

indicators.note: going on to means the boy's name follows the word for bask

parts.note: to sun oneself is to bask
Ken is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy goes off to sunbathe and ends up underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying below the surface, like a wreck, has gone down and is submerged.
